name: Tech Ethics
desc: Mitigating and avoiding the potential negative effects of technology on society.

resources.name: Children & AI Design Code
resources.desc: a process to identify, evaluate, and mitigate the known risks of AI to children and prepare for the known unknowns. The 5rights Foundation have also published Tick to Agree – Age appropriate presentation of published terms.

resources.name: Civic AI - 6-Pack of Care
resources.desc: AI alignment that asks who gets heard, who is accountable, how failures are repaired, and when a system should stop. Alignment is not solved once. It is maintained in public.

resources.name: Consequence Scanning
resources.desc: A new agile event that fits into an iterative development cadence. A way to think about the potential impact of a product or service on people and society early on in the development cycle.

resources.name: IDEO's AI ethics cards
resources.desc: Activities to "help guide an ethically responsible, culturally considerate, and humanistic approach to designing with data."

resources.name: Permacomputing design principles
resources.desc: Permacomputing is both a concept and a community of practice oriented around issues of resilience and regenerativity in computer and network technology inspired by permaculture.

resources.name: Manifesto for a Humane Web
resources.desc: "A personal response to the current state of the web \[...\] a statement of intent and a call to arms, inviting you, the reader, to go forth and build humane websites, and to resist the erosion of the web we know and love."

resources.name: The ResponsibleTech.Work framework
resources.desc: An open-source framework developed by tech workers for tech workers. It equips tech workers with practical tools for more responsible product development.

resources.name: Spotify Ethics Guild's ethics assessment
resources.desc: A tool for identifying ethical considerations when designing a product or service.

resources.name: Sweet summer child score
resources.desc: An interactive quiz to identify the possibility of harm to people and communities by a socio-technical system.

resources.name: Tethix Elemental Sparks
resources.desc: Printouts for origami chatterboxes to spark conversations about AI, data, fairness, and other sociotechnical challenges.

resources.name: The Tarot Cards of Tech
resources.desc: A set of questions designed to help creators more fully consider the impact of technology.

resources.name: Tech Won't Save Us podcast
resources.desc: Tech Won't Save Us challenges the notion that tech alone can drive our world forward by showing that tech is inherently political and ignoring that has serious consequences. It encourages listeners to think about how we can move beyond oppressive tech and towards tech for genuine public good.

resources.name: Revolution.Social podcast
resources.desc: A podcast about the future of social media built on permissionless open protocols, hosted by Twitter's first employee, Rabble a.k.a. Evan Henshaw-Plath. Hear what's possible when social platforms and content are no longer owned by corporations.

resources.name: Machine Ethics Podcast
resources.desc: Conversations on AI Ethics: Interrogating technology, artificial intelligence and society.

resources.name: Ethics, Technology + Public Policy for Practitioners
resources.desc: An online course from Stanford University covering the ethical and social challenges that the technology sector faces throughout product and operational decision-making.

resources.name: ACM SIGCAS
resources.desc: The Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) Special Interest Group that addresses the social and ethical consequences of widespread computer usage.

resources.name: The Ada Lovelace Institute
resources.desc: An independent research institute with a mission to ensure data and AI work for people and society.

resources.name: The Algorithmic Justice League
resources.desc: AJL raises awareness about the impacts of AI, undertakes empirical research, strengthens the most impacted communities, and galvanizes researchers, policy makers, and industry practitioners to mitigate AI harms and biases.

resources.name: All Tech Is Human
resources.desc: Bringing together people, organizations, and ideas to tackle wicked tech & society issues and co-create a tech future aligned with the public interest.

resources.name: Center for Humane Technology
resources.desc: Envisioning a world with technology that respects our attention, improves our well-being, and strengthens communities.

resources.name: The Design Justice Network
resources.desc: A home for people who are committed to embodying and practicing the Design Justice Network Principles.

resources.name: The Distributed AI Research Institute
resources.desc: The Distributed AI Research Institute is a space for independent, community-rooted AI research, free from Big Tech's pervasive influence.

resources.name: Foxglove
resources.desc: We stand up to tech giants and governments and for a future where technology is used to benefit everyone, not just the rich and powerful.

resources.name: The Minderoo Centre for Technology and Democracy
resources.desc: An independent team of researchers at the University of Cambridge who are radically rethinking the power relationships between digital technologies, society, and our planet.

resources.name: Omidyar Network: Responsible Technology
resources.desc: Social change venture that reimagines critical systems, and the ideas that govern them, to build more inclusive and equitable societies. Responsible technology is one of its three key focus areas.

resources.name: Organization for Ethical Source
resources.desc: Develops tools and standards to promote fair, ethical, and equitable outcomes for everyone who contributes to, benefits from, or is impacted by open source technologies.

resources.name: Tethix
resources.desc: "Tech ethics that makes you smile".

resources.name: Amazon Employees for Climate Justice
resources.desc: Amazon employees applying pressure on Amazon to redefine what it means to be a responsible company in the era of the climate crisis.

resources.name: No Tech For Apartheid
resources.desc: a worker-led campaign of Google and Amazon workers organizing against the companies' $1B Project Nimbus cloud computing contract with the Israeli government and military (see also No Azure for Apartheid).

resources.name: No Tech for ICE
resources.desc: fighting against the tech corporations fueling ICE disappearances, raids and the growing surveillance state.

resources.name: Deceptive Patterns
resources.desc: cataloging and exposing tricks used in websites and apps that make you do things that you didn't mean to, like buying or signing up for something.
